title: 4. PKI — The Trust Framework
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L08: Cryptography 2 (Asymmetric, PKI, TLS, Signatures): 4. PKI — The Trust Framework .

blocks.text: Alice receives "Bob's public key." How does she know it really belongs to Bob and not Mallory? Answer: a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) signs Bob's key + identity into a certificate.

rows: Top trust anchor; kept offline; pre-installed in OS/browser
Server attaches fresh OCSP response to handshake
Public append-only log of every issued cert

blocks.text: `` Root CA (offline) / \ Intermediate 1 Intermediate 2 / | | \ Server certs User certs ``

items: DigiNotar (2011) — CA hacked; 531 fraudulent certs incl. *.google.com; CA bankrupt within 6 weeks
Symantec (2017) — misissuance crisis; Chrome distrusted entire PKI

blocks.text: If a CA's private key leaks, every cert it ever signed is suspect. That's why root CAs are stored in offline HSMs in vaults.

attribution: Course: ICCS423 | Source: Thoth Library (cryptography/) + RAG | Target: 3rd-4th year CS | Date: 2026-05-03
cheatsheet: Root CA: Top trust anchor; kept offline; pre-installed in OS/browser
Intermediate CA: Issues end-entity certificates online
Registration Authority (RA): Verifies identity before CA issues
OCSP Stapling: Server attaches fresh OCSP response to handshake
CT Log: Public append-only log of every issued cert
